records.applicability_notes: GIBREP: all ships of 300 GT and over; all ships carrying hazardous or potentially polluting cargo; towing/pushing; vessels under 300 GT using lanes to fish or the separation zone in emergency. Cross-Strait scheduled ferries may have special arrangements.
records.tss_identity_note: Listed as amended scheme in COLREG.2/Circ.40 (implemented 24 Nov 1994) and COLREG.2/Circ.58 (MSC 82, implemented 1 July 2007); MSC.300(87) (2010) refers to the amended TSS within the GIBREP area. Earlier original adoption not traced.
records.vts_relationship_basis: MSC.300(87) annex 3.5.1: both Tarifa and Tangier centres monitor navigation in the TSS using radar and AIS; S11 confirms CCS Tarifa ('Tarifa Tráfico') provides the maritime traffic service in the Strait.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: GIBREP area (005°58'W to 005°15'W) includes the amended TSS (MSC.300(87) annex 2.1).
records.complexity_reason: Two-State shared VTS and mandatory SOLAS V/11 reporting with direction-dependent reporting centres.
records.open_questions: Lead (news/petition, not primary) that Tarifa Tráfico functions were moved provisionally to CCS Algeciras; not verified because salvamentomaritimo.es returned HTTP 503. Current VHF channels should be rechecked against the latest ALRS/Spanish NtM.

records.voluntary_reporting: Voluntary reporting system at Cabo de Gata (RPT-cabo-de-gata-voluntary); details not retrieved.
records.tss_identity_note: New scheme in COLREG.2/Circ.44 (MSC 69, implemented 1 Dec 1998); amended by COLREG.2/Circ.57 (MSC 81, implemented 1 Dec 2006). Amended scheme includes an inshore traffic zone.
records.vts_relationship_basis: S11 (Ministry of Transport, Feb 2025): Salvamento Marítimo is responsible for controlling traffic safety in the DST of Cabo de Gata; S12 (2015) counts vessels identified passing the Cabo de Gata DST. Controlling centre (CCS Almería) is lead only.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: S11 states Spain's mandatory reporting systems are at Fisterra and the Strait of Gibraltar (plus Canarias PSSA) 'mientras que en el cabo de Gata existe un sistema de notificación voluntaria'. Absence of mandatory reporting positively stated by an official source.
records.complexity_reason: Single-State VTS monitoring with voluntary reporting only.
records.open_questions: Confirm centre name (CCS Almería), call sign and VHF channel from Salvamento Marítimo (site returned HTTP 503) or ALRS Vol 6.

records.tss_identity_note: New scheme in COLREG.2/Circ.52 (MSC 76, implemented 1 July 2003). S11 (2025) lists cabo de Palos among Spain's existing DSTs.
records.vts_relationship_basis: S11 lists the DSTs Salvamento Marítimo controls as Fisterra, Tarifa, Cabo de Gata and Canarias, omitting Cabo de Palos, but the same article also states generally that DSTs are controlled by VTS assigned to Salvamento Marítimo. No source establishes CCS Cartagena coverage of the TSS.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: S11: 'En España existen sistemas de notificación obligatoria en Fisterra y en el estrecho de Gibraltar' (plus Canarias PSSA); Cabo de Palos not included. Moderate confidence: enumerative statement in an official publication rather than a formal complete list.
records.complexity_reason: Single-State TSS, no mandatory reporting, VTS coverage unclear.
records.open_questions: Does CCS Cartagena monitor the Palos TSS? salvamentomaritimo.es (HTTP 503) and ALRS not accessible.

records.source_label: Off Cape la Nao (Cabo de la Nao)
records.tss_identity_note: New scheme in COLREG.2/Circ.52 (MSC 76, implemented 1 July 2003); reference chart Spanish IHM chart 47. S11 (2025) lists cabo de la Nao among Spain's DSTs.
records.vts_relationship_basis: As for Cabo de Palos: S11 omits La Nao from the DSTs Salvamento Marítimo controls; no source establishes CCS Valencia coverage.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: S11 enumerates Spain's mandatory reporting systems (Fisterra, Gibraltar, Canarias PSSA); La Nao not included. Moderate confidence.
records.complexity_reason: Single-State TSS, no mandatory reporting, VTS coverage unclear.
records.open_questions: Does CCS Valencia monitor the La Nao TSS? Primary Salvamento Marítimo pages not accessible (HTTP 503).

records.official_name: North of Cani Island (Off Cani Island)
records.tss_identity_note: Tunisian scheme (Îles Cani, off Bizerte coast), not the Bonifacio Strait. Amended by COLREG.2/Circ.58 (MSC 82, implemented 1 July 2007) together with Off Cape Bon; reference chart 150-DST of the Tunisian Hydrographic and Oceanographic Service. Original scheme reported operating since 1 Aug 1970 (search snippet from NOAA document, lead only).
records.vts_relationship_basis: No Tunisian VTS or traffic monitoring centre covering the scheme found; searches returned only general coastal surveillance (RMAC) news.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: No IMO-adopted SRS for the area in S14 list; national reporting not researched to a primary source.
records.complexity_reason: Single-State TSS with no identified VTS or reporting.
records.open_questions: Tunisian Marine Marchande / SHOM Tunisie sources not found online. Region hint linking Cani Island to BONIFREP is wrong: BONIFREP (MSC.73(69)) is Corsica/Sardinia and not relevant here.

records.official_name: North of Cape Bon (Off Cape Bon)
records.tss_identity_note: Amended by COLREG.2/Circ.58 (MSC 82, implemented 1 July 2007) with Off Cani Island; reference chart 150-DST (Tunisia). Original scheme reported operating since 1 Aug 1970 (lead only).
records.vts_relationship_basis: No Tunisian VTS covering the scheme found.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: No IMO-adopted SRS listed for the area (S14); national reporting not established.
records.complexity_reason: Single-State TSS with no identified VTS or reporting.
records.open_questions: As for TSS-0070; Italian VTS/Pantelleria-Sicily Channel arrangements not researched (outside scheme).

records.tss_identity_note: New scheme in COLREG.2/Circ.67 (MSC 96, implemented 1 Dec 2016), between Cap Corse and Isola Capraia, with ITZ along the Corsican coast; reference charts SHOM 7013 and IIM 40.
records.vts_relationship_basis: Italian Guardia Costiera lists 11 VTS centres (S18, S19); none (Livorno not among them) is shown to cover the Corsica Channel. French coverage (CROSS MED) not researched to primary; CROSS is not a VTS.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: No IMO SRS for the Corsica Channel in S14 (2017 list); any later measure or national reporting not found.
records.complexity_reason: Bi-national scheme; no identified VTS, possible national arrangements.
records.open_questions: Italian MIT page on the 2015 Italy-France agreement (mit.gov.it/node/298) returned HTTP 503. Check whether a Livorno VTS has since been activated and whether France/Italy require reporting.

records.applicability_notes: ADRIREP (revised, from 1 Dec 2026): oil tankers 150 GT and above, ships 10,000 GT and above, any ship carrying hazardous cargo.
grouped_components: In the North Adriatic Sea - Eastern part
In the North Adriatic Sea - Western part
Precautionary area at the southern limits
records.source_label: In the Adriatic Sea: In the North Adriatic Sea
records.official_name: In the North Adriatic Sea (eastern part and western part), part of 'In the Adriatic Sea'
records.states: Italy, Croatia (with Slovenia in the wider system)
records.tss_identity_note: Adopted in COLREG.2/Circ.54 annex 3 (MSC 78, implemented 1 Dec 2004); western part amended by COLREG.2/Circ.58 (implemented 1 July 2007). Includes precautionary area at southern limits.
records.vts_relationship_basis: S20: VTS Croatia supervises application of the Adriatic TSS of COLREG.2/Circ.54 and 58 'u VTS području' (area incl. territorial sea and ZERP). Whether each component lies within the Croatian VTS area was not verified; no Italian VTS area covers this offshore scheme.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: ADRIREP covers the whole Adriatic north of 40°25'N (S13), which includes this scheme.
records.complexity_reason: Multi-State offshore scheme under a multi-authority mandatory reporting system.
records.open_questions: Plot components against Croatian ZERP/VTS chart 950 VTS to confirm coverage; confirm whether 2015 Croatian VTS description remains current. Later Adriatic TSS amendments after 2016 not checked (compilation ends c. Circ.68).

records.source_label: In the Adriatic Sea: Approaches to the Gulf of Trieste
records.tss_identity_note: Component of 'In the Adriatic Sea', COLREG.2/Circ.54 annex 3 (implemented 1 Dec 2004); separation line 45°07'.50N 013°00'.37E to 45°19'.00N 012°56'.87E.
records.vts_relationship_basis: Scheme lies offshore south-west of Istria, outside the VTS Trieste and Koper areas (S15, S16). VTS Croatia supervises Circ.54 schemes within its area (S20) but location of this component relative to that area not verified.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: Within ADRIREP area (whole Adriatic north of 40°25'N).
records.complexity_reason: Multi-State approach scheme; VTS responsibility unclear; mandatory ADRIREP.
records.open_questions: Confirm which State's waters and VTS area contain this component.

records.applicability_notes: Venice VTS participation mandatory for vessels of 300 GT and upwards (S17); ADRIREP categories as in RPT-adrirep.
records.source_label: In the Adriatic Sea: Approaches to the Gulf of Venice
records.tss_identity_note: Component of 'In the Adriatic Sea', COLREG.2/Circ.54 annex 3 (implemented 1 Dec 2004); separation zone amended by COLREG.2/Circ.58 (implemented 1 July 2007).
records.vts_relationship_basis: Direct approach: TSS northern terminus (c. 45°10'-45°14'N, 012°29'-012°39'E, S4) adjoins the Venice VTS area outer limit B-C (45°08.4'N 012°25.7'E to 45°16.0'N 012°35.0'E, S17), and participating vessels must call Venice VTS 5 NM outside that limit, i.e. while in the TSS. Coverage inferred by comparing coordinates from two primary sources; the manual does not say in words that the VTS covers the TSS.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: Within ADRIREP area; Venice MRSC and VTS Venezia are ADRIREP authorities (S13, S17).
records.complexity_reason: Single-State approach scheme leading to a mandatory VTS, plus ADRIREP.
records.open_questions: Venice manual dated 2017; check current edition. Reviewer to confirm the direct-approach judgement.

records.applicability_notes: Koper VTS: ships of 300 GT and upwards; fishing, traditional and recreational craft of 45 m and upwards; warships and government vessels exempt. VTS Trieste: 300 GT and over; pleasure/traditional craft 45 m and over.
grouped_components: Precautionary area in the Gulf of Trieste
records.source_label: In the Adriatic Sea: In the Gulf of Trieste and approaches to/from Koper
records.official_name: In the Gulf of Trieste; Approaches to/from Koper (with precautionary area in the Gulf of Trieste)
records.states: Slovenia, Italy (Croatia party to trilateral scheme)
records.tss_identity_note: Components of 'In the Adriatic Sea', COLREG.2/Circ.54 annex 3 (implemented 1 Dec 2004). Label groups two schemes plus a precautionary area.
records.vts_relationship_basis: Koper VTS manual section 7.1 describes both TSS and requires vessels in its area to use the lanes (S15). VTS Trieste manual: 'Nell'Area VTS di Trieste è ricompreso lo schema obbligatorio di separazione del traffico ... Golfo di Trieste' (S16). Each covers the part within its national waters.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: Within ADRIREP area; MRCC Koper and VTS Trieste are ADRIREP authorities (S13). Separate mandatory VTS reports to Koper VTS (entry/exit, 1 h before entry) and VTS Trieste are VTS duties, not separate schemes.
records.complexity_reason: Three-State area with two national VTS and ADRIREP.
records.open_questions: Croatian role (VTS Croatia/Umag) in the Gulf of Trieste not checked.

records.applicability_notes: VTS Trieste participation mandatory for ships of 300 GT and over etc.
records.source_label: In the Adriatic Sea: Approaches to/from Monfalcone
records.tss_identity_note: Component of 'In the Adriatic Sea', COLREG.2/Circ.54 annex 3 (implemented 1 Dec 2004); amended scheme per COLREG.2/Circ.58 referenced in VTS Trieste manual.
records.vts_relationship_basis: VTS Trieste area limits were set taking account of the TSS 'nella parte finale di ingresso/uscita dal porto di Monfalcone', and the manual states the Monfalcone TSS is included within the VTS area (S16).
records.reporting_relationship_basis: Within ADRIREP area; VTS Trieste is an ADRIREP authority (S13).
records.open_questions: Confirm whether all of the Monfalcone TSS or only its final part lies in the VTS area.

records.source_label: Saronicos Gulf (Saronikós Kólpos, in the Approaches to Piraiévs)
records.tss_identity_note: Existence as an IMO-adopted TSS evidenced by the 1991 COLREG.2 circular cancelling its inshore traffic zone (implemented 19 April 1991); original adoption instrument and current status not verified.
records.vts_relationship_basis: Lead only (S24): VTS in Piraeus linked to national VTMIS covering the wider Piraeus sea area. No primary source on VTS area or TSS coverage (hcg.gr HTTP 403).
records.reporting_relationship_basis: No IMO SRS for Greece in S14; Greek national VTS participation rules seen only in search snippets (lead).
records.complexity_reason: Busy port approach likely with VTS; evidence incomplete.
records.open_questions: Obtain Hellenic Coast Guard VTS Piraeus regulation/ALRS entry; confirm TSS still current in Ships' Routeing (operational status provisional).

records.source_label: In the approaches to the port of Thessaloníki
records.official_name: In the approaches to the Port of Thessaloniki
records.tss_identity_note: New scheme in COLREG.2/Circ.60 (MSC 85, implemented 1 June 2009).
records.vts_relationship_basis: No source found for a Thessaloniki VTS; lead S24 lists Greek VTS at Piraeus, Patras, Igoumenitsa and Kerkyra only (undated, not primary).
records.reporting_relationship_basis: No IMO SRS; national reporting not established.
records.complexity_reason: Single-State port approach TSS; VTS status unknown.
records.open_questions: Check Hellenic Coast Guard for any Thessaloniki VTS (planned or operational) and port reporting duties.

records.applicability_notes: SP-1: ships carrying dangerous cargo and ships of 500 GT and over (24 h before entry); position and calling-in point reports: ships of 20 m and over.
records.tss_identity_note: Adopted by MSC 63, COLREG.2/Circ.40 (implemented 24 Nov 1994), together with 'Strait of Istanbul', 'Strait of Istanbul - South Approach and Sea of Marmara', 'Strait of Canakkale' and its South-West Approach. National regulation (2019) Art. 4 sets the TSS limits in the north at 41°20'.944 N. This record covers the North Approach only; linked components to be resolved in their own records.
records.vts_relationship_basis: Turkish Straits Maritime Traffic Regulation 2019, Art. 4-5: TSS in the Turkish Straits and their approaches (northern limit 41°20'.944 N) with TBGTH established for application and supervision of the TSS and reporting system; S21 confirms TSVTS operational since 2003 with İstanbul centre.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: Regulation Art. 7: SP-2 2 h or 20 NM before entering the Istanbul Strait and position report 5 NM before the entrance, i.e. in the North Approach. National mandatory system, not IMO-adopted.
records.complexity_reason: Linked multi-segment strait regime with national VTS, mandatory national reporting and Montreux Convention context.
records.open_questions: Sector names/channels (Türkeli etc.) not confirmed from a primary source; Regulation read from scanned Resmî Gazete images (pages 2, 3, 5 only); 2020 amendments not checked.

method_notes: Access problems: salvamentomaritimo.es and mit.gov.it returned HTTP 503 (and curl TLS chain errors); hcg.gr returned 403; mevzuat.gov.tr served a script page, but the Resmî Gazete scanned PDF was read via page images (no OCR available). Useful sources: Transportstyrelsen's compiled COLREG.2 circulars PDF (IMO TSS adoption/implementation dates to c. 2016), IMO resolution PDFs on wwwcdn.imo.org, Guardia Costiera VTS manuals page (official list of 11 Italian VTS with manuals), Slovenian URSP Koper VTS manual, HHI Croatian VTS supplement, Spanish Ministry 'Los DST' article (Feb 2025) which enumerates Spanish controlled DSTs and mandatory reporting. Suggested changes: obtain ALRS Vol 6 or national NtM annual editions for Spain, Greece and Tunisia; plot TSS coordinates against VTS area limits systematically for offshore Adriatic components.
